cards.text: Isaiah, God's prophet, is speaking. He opens with "Behold," which is a prophet's way of saying STOP SCROLLING AND LOOK. And what he wants you to look at is a king.

cards.question: Isaiah says a king is coming. How will this king reign?
Along with this king, Isaiah says princes will rule with justice. True or false?

cards.text: Isaiah says each of these leaders will be "like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in an arid land." Friend, that's not a leader. That's a whole REST STOP.

cards.question: Shelter, refuge, water and shade. What do Isaiah's pictures of these leaders have in common?

answers.text: They keep people at a distance

cards.text: Then Isaiah says things change for the people too, starting with their eyes and ears. No more me nodding "mm-hmm" while I'm staring at the oven timer.

cards.question: Isaiah says the ears of those who hear will still refuse to listen. True or false?

cards.text: Next Isaiah gets to the mind and the mouth, and the stammering tongue "will speak clearly and fluently." Friend, my first day with a baker I said, "Welcome to the... uh... the cookie... the bakery is cookies."

cards.question: Isaiah says the mind of the rash will change too. What will it do?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says the honor is about to go where it belongs. No more Employee of the Month for the guy who takes credit for the whole team's batch.

cards.question: Isaiah says no longer will a ___ be called noble, nor a scoundrel be respected.

cards.text: Isaiah describes the fool. His mind plots iniquity, and he "speaks falsely about the LORD."

cards.question: Isaiah says the fool leaves the ___ empty and deprives the ___ of drink.

cards.text: Then comes the scoundrel, and his weapons are destructive. He hatches plots to destroy the poor with lies.

cards.question: Isaiah says the scoundrel only goes after the poor when their plea is unfair. True or false?

cards.text: But then Isaiah flips it. After all that plotting, here comes the noble man, and he "makes honorable plans."

cards.question: Isaiah says a noble man makes honorable plans and stands up for ___ causes.

cards.text: Now Isaiah calls out, "Stand up, you complacent women; listen to me." He calls them overconfident, and friend, that's me napping on my gold base with a batch still in the oven.

cards.question: Isaiah tells these overconfident women they will tremble. How soon?
Isaiah tells these secure ones they will tremble, because the grape harvest will ___ and the fruit harvest will not arrive.

cards.text: So Isaiah tells them to shudder and tremble, to strip and put sackcloth around their waists.

cards.question: Isaiah tells these women to beat their breasts in grief. What are they grieving?

answers.text: The pleasant fields and fruitful vines
A king who has fallen in battle

cards.text: And they mourn for "the land of my people, overgrown with thorns and briers," even every house of merriment in the city of revelry. The party houses are getting thorns.

cards.question: With thorns taking over the land, Isaiah says the palace and the busy city will stay full of people. True or false?

cards.text: The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever, "the delight of wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks." From royal palace to donkey hangout, and the donkeys are leaving FIVE-STAR reviews.
But hold on, friend. That "forever" comes with an "until."

cards.question: Isaiah says the ruin lasts until something is "poured out upon us from on high." What is poured out?
Once the Spirit is poured out, Isaiah says the desert will stay dry and empty. True or false?

cards.text: Isaiah says the desert will be an orchard, "and the orchard will seem like a forest." Friend, I know that kind of upgrade, because I went from the back of a dusty junk drawer to a WHOLE BAKERY.

cards.question: Isaiah says ___ will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field.

cards.text: Then Isaiah tells what all that righteousness produces.

cards.question: Isaiah says the work of righteousness will be ___ and the service of righteousness will be quiet ___ forever.

cards.text: Quiet confidence forever. Friend, I've got the confidence, but quiet? I have NEVER been quiet a day in my life.

cards.question: Isaiah says "my people" will keep moving from place to place with no rest. True or false?

cards.text: Then comes a sudden turn: "But hail will level the forest, and the city will sink to the depths."

cards.question: Isaiah ends with a blessing. Who does he call blessed?

answers.text: Those who sow beside abundant waters
Those who build behind high walls
Those who store grain in barns

cards.text: Those blessed sowers let the ox and donkey range freely, and that's where Isaiah ends. Me? I let my sprinkles range freely ONE time, and I'm still finding them.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "speaks falsely about the LORD.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 16 quotes "makes honorable plans.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "the delight of wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card says who is speaking (Isaiah) but never says who he is speaking to, and gives no context for what is going on. The passage picks up right after Isaiah 31, so the baker starts with no setting.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: "The honor is about to go where it belongs" adds nearness in time. Verse 5 only says "No longer will," with no time given. It also stretches the verse: verse 5 says fools and scoundrels stop being honored, not that honor goes somewhere else.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The story card is a plain paraphrase with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Together with card 14, this leaves two dry cards in a row in the middle of the stop.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The story card is a plain paraphrase of verse 7 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: "So Isaiah tells them..." makes verse 11 a result of verse 10. The text gives no "therefore" and leaves the connection open. The card is also a bare paraphrase with no voice.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "And they mourn for..." states as fact that the women mourn. Verses 12–13 are Isaiah's command ("Beat your breasts for..."), and the text never says they do it.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "The party houses are getting thorns" stretches verse 13. The thorns and briers are on the land. The houses of merriment are named as something else to mourn for, not as overgrown.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "The donkeys are leaving FIVE-STAR reviews" mixes a modern image into the Bible scene itself instead of using a separate everyday comparison. "From royal palace to donkey hangout" also misplaces the detail: verse 14 says the hill and watchtower become the delight of wild donkeys, while the palace is forsaken.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This card adds nothing new from the passage. It repeats "quiet confidence forever," which card 15 already asked, just to set up a joke, so it doesn't move the baker forward. The joke "I have NEVER been quiet a day in my life" also contradicts his backstory, where in the drawer he "didn't talk much. He didn't joke at all."

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The joke states something about Papa Dorin's past that conflicts with his established backstory (going quiet in the junk drawer).

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
